notes.title: Hotfix Update 1.2.8.14462 (Experimental)
notes.content:
[p]Hello Seedlings,  We have a patch for you today in the Experimental Branch. Check out the changelog at the bottom of this post for the full details.  [/p][p][/p][p][b]How to get the Experimental Build installed:[/b]

In your Steam library, right-click and access properties for Kynseed.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/697897a992d29c092ff7630e3d71f8249509a4e9.png"][/img][/p][p]Under the Betas tab, select Experimental from the dropdown.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/f882bca826599025e9a3fd4246f03a8b7beedd07.png"][/img]This should now update and replace the build with this version. You can return to the normal build by choosing None for the Beta Participation options.


[b]Things to note:[/b]

Installing this build will overwrite your current version of Kynseed. Existing saves stay in the Saves folder, whilst Experimental saves go into a new folder.

If you want to return to the previous build, switch back to the default branch on Steam, where your previous saves will be intact. You won't be able to load your Experimental saves into the default branch.


[b]How to get in touch:[/b]

We welcome any feedback that can help us improve - [url="https://bugs@pixelcountstudios.com"]bugs@pixelcountstudios.com[/url] or via our Discord server at [url="https://discord.gg/pixelcount"]discord.gg/pixelcount[/url]


That is it for now. Thank you for reading this post and for still being on this Quillian journey with us.


All the best,

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/b3c6d0707c39c9f57f6dd14a08fd54cf11936db3.png"][/img]PixelCount   [/p][p][/p][p][b]Experimental Changelog 1.2.8.14462:[/b] [/p][p][/p][p]❌ Fix for combat loadouts not loading on save games [/p][p]❌ Fix for gifting towards skills not working consistently on dpad[/p][p]❌ Fix for recipe book tabs skipping on controller[/p][p]❌ Fix for overcast clouds appearing in Tir Na Nog[/p][p]❌ Fix for Creek n Coop crash[/p][p]❌ Fix for player saves after defeating Jabberwock in Stonecrown not tracking state correctly[/p][p]❌ Fix for exorcism task ghosts in Copperpot being in non-interactable spots[/p]

notes.title: New patch available in Experimental
notes.content:
Hello Seedlings,

We have a big patch for you today in the Experimental Branch: bug fixes, community-requested improvements, and some new bits and pieces. Check out the changelog at the bottom of this post for the full details.

As a general update for you, we've been doing a lot of behind-the-scenes work on getting the game future-proof for translations as well as some other new developments, news of which we are working on giving you this autumn. It has been a busy time for the five of us as we iron out issues and revisit code that was first written years ago! Of particular note is the dusting off, rebuilding, and polishing of how we handle text in the game. With over 310,000 words, there is a lot to handle, and this has made edits and especially adding new languages harder than it might have been had we known how many words we'd end up having when we started! Phew! Pause for breath..

We have two new languages in this Experimental - French and Korean. We started with French as it was the most familiar language. Korean we chose for the use of glyphs in the game. We are also conscious that there are community-created language mods out there, which may be broken by the new way we handle text, one of the most popular of which is Korean, so we thought we'd better get our beta out as soon as possible. Our experimental translations feature text crafted through a collaborative effort involving professional translators, community contributors, and advanced AI technology. With such a word count, we strive for accuracy and clarity, though some nuances may vary. We appreciate your understanding and welcome any feedback that can help us improve - bugs@pixelcountstudios.com or via our Discord server at discord.gg/pixelcount


[b]How to get the Experimental Build installed:[/b]

In your Steam library, right-click and access properties for Kynseed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/697897a992d29c092ff7630e3d71f8249509a4e9.png[/img]

Under the Betas tab, select Experimental from the dropdown.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/f882bca826599025e9a3fd4246f03a8b7beedd07.png[/img]

This should now update and replace the build with this version. You can return to the normal build by choosing None for the Beta Participation options.


[b]Things to note:[/b]

Installing this build will overwrite your current version of Kynseed. Existing saves stay in the Saves folder, whilst Experimental saves go into a new folder.

If you want to return to the previous build, switch back to the default branch on Steam, where your previous saves will be intact. You won't be able to load your Experimental saves into the default branch.


[b]How to get in touch:[/b]

We welcome any feedback that can help us improve - bugs@pixelcountstudios.com or via our Discord server at discord.gg/pixelcount


That is it for now. Thank you for reading this post and for still being on this Quillian journey with us.


All the best,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/b3c6d0707c39c9f57f6dd14a08fd54cf11936db3.png[/img]
PixelCount

notes.title: Big Build Update Out Now!
notes.content:
1.1.0.11901


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/d2cc6bd52e35418d21899128831d23553e80b101.png[/img]


+ [b]Customisation[/b]
	+ Customise the look of your farm interior and exterior.
	+ Spend money to unlock more plots on the farm.
	+ Unlock more customisations by playing the game.  These can be bought or gained from challenges and other sources around the world.
	+ A certain Fairweather item might also give you a further area to customise…

+ [b]Friends & Family Builds[/b]
	+ Build additional structures for your farm that provide benefits or give shelter to your animals.
	+ Repair structures like bridges to gain access to new areas or statues/stalls to make travel and commerce easier.
	+ Repair houses that can be destroyed by the encroaching evil creatures of the land.
        + New Axe and choppable trees for wood collection
	+ New Stone resource.

+ [b]Totems[/b]
	+ Many areas can now be infiltrated by monsters that place a totem which blocks resources and any F&F building in the area.
	+ Through a mini combat room clear the rifts and totem to restore the area and gain rewards.
	+ Eligible family can clear totems through gathering in that location.

+ [b]Progress Screen[/b]
	+ Track all your progress through this screen with a picture that fills in as you go.
	+ Challenges gives over 400 challenges to complete throughout all aspects of the game with rewards of money/items and customisation unlocks.
	+ Items screen gives a breakdown of how many you have found, total collected and the highest rating acquired.
	+ Relationship screen tracks all current npcs and your relationship with them.
	+ Story/Event keeps a history of parts of the game you have already discovered.
	+ Shops gives a brief overview of how your shops are doing.
	+ Customisation catalogue shows you all items you can unlock and what activities will unlock them.

+ [b]Story Pacing[/b]
	+ Some new tasks added with new characters and a new area and combat wood to unlock.
	+ Additional cutscenes during childhood.
	+ The flow of the game has been improved from start to finish to have a gentler pace unlocking as you learn the ways of the land.

+ [b]New Noticeboard Tasks[/b]
	+ Races
	+ Treasure Hunts
	+ Paranormal Activity

+[b] NPC improvements[/b]
	+ A new talent system means each NPC, including your children, has their own skill which can be used to your benefit.
	+ New dialogue has been added for reactions to you and relative to their level of friendship
	+ Some NPCs now have cutscenes as your relationship grows with them.
	+ The type of an NPC’s like/dislike can now be seen on their info to make for more targeted gifting.
	+ NPCs now travel between levels and have had other AI tweaks.
	+ Your previous family can visit from time to time at your farm.

+ [b]Batch Crafting[/b]
	+ After crafting 3 of a given item type you unlock the ability to craft in batches making up to 10 at once if you have the ingredients for them.

+ [b]Proverb acquiring[/b]
	+ These can be automatically given based on collecting the items at 5/10/15 of the item.
	+ Proverbs found in the world are now context based to what skills/recipes and items in the level you might not have found yet.
	+ For some items collecting 20 will also unlock the ability to place them through customisation.

+ [b]Discovering Star Ratings[/b]
	+ Picking up an item will now reveal one of the rating conditions in effect.
	+ Review the info on the proverb tab or in the items page of the progress screen and you may be able to deduce the other ratings!

+ [b]Instant Message System[/b]
	+ Alerts the player to various events/tasks in the game.
	+ Also provides shop alerts if you are running low on stock.

+ [b]Misc[/b]
	+ Kynseed Tree keeps growing.
	+ Rumble added for controllers.
	+ The apothecary can now craft combat items in a similar way to cures.
	+ Good store ledger clearer on how transactions are making money/rep.
	+ On the Character screen can select stats/traits/talents and press a key for more info on them.
	+ Can choose the initial depth (difficulty level) on combat runs, the higher depths unlock as you complete a run reaching that depth.
	+ Task to earn a new fae pet.
	~ Friendship points has a new popup that shows where you are getting bonus points from.
	~ Update pass on all the text.

~ [b]Balance Adjustments[/b]
	~ Skill requirements adjusted.
	~ More renown given for completing story and extra is given for all sources in the later game.
	~ Tools lower xp to level.
	~ Prices on items are up to make rating modifiers more effective.
	~ Brounie offerings removed as it clashed with totems and customisation.
	~ Goddess offerings randomly paired each week.
	~ Fish are weighted to appear more when their exact conditions occur.
	~ Combat runs are slightly shorter and puzzle rooms are not guaranteed.
	~ Noticeboard task rewards are a bit more generous.
	~ Extra perk points at the higher levels of shops after all the shopper types are unlocked.

[b]Fixes[/b]
! Various level collision/layering issues.
! Fixed issues where certain events would not trigger.
! Fixed Issues with lost items not spawning.
! Removed holes from giant vegetables.
! Aurore Boon correctly grants double herb in all cases.
! Animal likes adjusted.
! Rating conditions adjusted for Moxy/Offals Tench.
! Pig/Sheep riding anims redone.
! Fixed issues with dates to do with date spots and items gifted.
! Fixed Good store shops not making sales if you use a campfire in the same level.
! Fixed Good store shoppers not buying items at higher star rating prices.
! Fixed Good store staff pricing new items at 1 brass (now uses a number around the base price which could be a bit lower or higher).
! Collect honey order applies rating conditions.
! Cooking orders results apply ratings based on ingredients.
! Missing chickens not moving to the next step in some cases on returning the chickens.
! Chickens around the levels given names.
! Good store perk for outdoor item appears in the right place and gives star rated items.
! 4 missing recipes located.
! “In the morning” rating condition now includes dawn.
! Turning on and off lights could leave them lit with no light.
! Bees in jars weren’t selectable in combat.
! Wearing harvest task issues where it wouldn’t complete.

notes.title: Big Build Update Out Now!
notes.content:
Hi Seedlings!

Welcome to the Big Build Update!

Your game should now have updated, if not check your library and you can do it manually from there.

We've spent the last year since release reviewing player comments and have developed a host of new features and improvements that we think make the game even better.

There is now farm customisation, building projects with friends and family, new combat totems that Hobs put up around Quill, story cut-scenes, loads of new NPC chat and conversation, a beautiful new progress screen, hundreds of new challenges, improvements to the flow and gating of the game and loads of other quality of life additions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/72e4866efbede0a006eb2dda3b593ec287f66517.png[/img]

With the new improvements, we suggest you start a brand new character to experience the many additions to their fullest.

Your previous game(s) will load, though, so you can jump back in and explore the changes that way if you prefer. However, you'd miss out on some gating and story additions.

However you decide to play, we hope you enjoy this new update. It has been a true labour of love for our little team to create it, but we always felt it was worth the effort to respect the engagement and goodwill we've had from all of you since we launched.

Head to our [url=https://discord.com/invite/pixelcount]Discord[/url]  for help with questions and advice, or pop comments below and we will endeavour to answer them.



All the best,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/b3c6d0707c39c9f57f6dd14a08fd54cf11936db3.png[/img]

PixelCount

notes.title: Big Build Update goes Experimental
notes.content:
Hi Seedlings!

We've just pressed the button to make our latest update available as an Experimental Build.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/9dfbf6a0e4f534c5888513e90f3c57ce07ec6baa.png[/img]

We’ve spent the last year since release reviewing player comments and have come up with a host of new features and improvements which we think make the game even better. 

[b]What to try[/b]:

[list]
[*] Start a new game. We’ve changed the content a lot, so that will be the only way to fully experience all that is new.
[*] Try Customising your farm. This is gated at the very start, but not long into the Prologue, you can play about with this much-requested feature. Turn the music up when doing so to hear a new track!
[*] Check out the new Friends & Family gameplay, which will have you organising friendly villagers to repair ruined buildings and bridges.
[*] When you hit Renown Level 3, you will see Hobs putting up evil Totems around the land. These are new combat challenges with great loot rewards.
[*] Spend some time playing with the beautiful new Progress Screen. This, we believe, really helps tie together the whole game experience.
[*] Try the revised Skill Tree system - we’ve tried to make it easier to unlock some skills so that your progression is faster.
[/list]

[b]What to expect[/b]:

[list]
[*] There is a lot more variety when chatting with NPCs.
[*] Clearer clues to what NPCs need in their lives.
[*] New task types.
[*] New cut-scenes, both for the player’s story and NPC stories.
[/list]

[b]Things to note[/b]:

[list]
[*] Installing this build will overwrite your current version of Kynseed. Existing saves stay in the Saves folder, whilst Experimental saves go into a new folder.
[*] If you want to return to the previous build, switch back to the default branch on Steam, where your previous saves will be intact. You won’t be able to load your Experimental saves into the default branch.
[*] We have bugs. We are working through them right now. If you spot any big ones, let us know - specifically crashes. We don’t see many crashes these days, but if you see one:
[/list]
[olist]
[*] Take a screenshot of the red crash screen using the Snipping tool in Windows and send it to us via the channel on Discord, or by email at bugs@pixelcountstudios.com.
[*] Also, send us your latest save, found in Kynseed/ExperimentalSaves.
[*] And finally, send us the latest file in Kynseed/Logs.
[/olist]

There is more balance work to be done, for instance, on item prices, Friendship Points and Renown levels, and a few other relationship and story tweaks we are a bit behind on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/8dc52d026a2b82ecb4a570aa246417448f654b2e.png[/img]
This player needs plenty of friends to complete her farm vision...

[hr][/hr]
[b]How to get the Experimental Build installed[/b]:

In your steam library right click and access properties for Kynseed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/697897a992d29c092ff7630e3d71f8249509a4e9.png[/img]

Under the Betas tab, select Experimental from the dropdown.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/f882bca826599025e9a3fd4246f03a8b7beedd07.png[/img]

This should now update and replace the build with this version. You can return to the normal build by choosing None for the Beta Participation options.

[b]How to get in touch[/b]:

Our Community Manager has set up a dedicated channel on PixelCount’s [url=https://discord.com/invite/pixelcount]Discord[/url] called Experimental Build. If Discord is not your thing, you can email us at bugs@pixelcountstudios.com.



That is it. Once again, thank you for being one of our much-loved community members in the first place, but even bigger thanks if you decide to take a quick look at this build preview. We hope you like it.



All the best,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/b3c6d0707c39c9f57f6dd14a08fd54cf11936db3.png[/img]

PixelCount

notes.title: Development Update - December 2023
notes.content:
Hello Seedlings!

A dev update to close out the year.

The Big Build Update is now in the hands of a select group of our Discord Community members to do a pre-experimental wander around Quill. They are generally customising their farms, repairing houses and checking out the new features.

So far, we've had some great feedback, with a mix of the odd crash, some bugs, some fantastic ideas and general heartwarming positivity.

The Holiday season has come at just the wrong time for getting the Experimental out for everyone as we need to take a little break to spend some time with our families. A couple of us will continue testing and coding between Christmas and the New Year, and we will all be back beavering away on Jan 2nd.

We occasionally get bugs that send us down rabbit holes, wondering, 'What if that was a game feature?'. These tend to be an easy-to-take distraction from getting our to-do lists done! Here are two recent bugs that made us laugh and wonder equally!

First up, whilst tweaking the new Customisation Catalogue, the bug spirits, if there are such a thing, seem to suggest new plantable types - Bottle Bushes, anyone?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/65e73f1e603ad22acd252f829eadc376a5827eef.png[/img]

Then, and this is something we admit is interestingly compelling, having Butterscotch follow you around! Let me say now: this ain't happening anytime soon, but it would be handy for any immediate Milk Delivery requests you might get!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/6b72a19d6404f31b7b4d6e03696c5db78e45ea3b.gif[/img]

We've also spotted what looks like Santa's present store outside Willowdown Farm - courtesy of our soon to be released Customisation mode, of course.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/6f796bce8eae32c6ad81c2d13c263b7bc3dd8197.png[/img]

That's it for now. All that is left to say is we hope you all have lovely Christmas and New Year celebrations and that you get some time to do some gaming, perhaps a bit of Kynseed, along with all the other great games that have come out recently.



All the best,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/b3c6d0707c39c9f57f6dd14a08fd54cf11936db3.png[/img]

PixelCount

notes.title: Development Update - November 2023
notes.content:
Hello Seedlings!

A dev update for you. 

Development on The Big Build has continued at full steam, and as we mentioned previously, we plan to release an Experimental build for you all to play.

However, as with bug-fixing logic, sometimes when you fix one, you add two more... so we still have issues that we’d prefer to iron out, before we share it with you, but we promise it’ll be worth the wait.  As for exact timeline we don't feel confident enough to share an exact date right now but it's looking like being within the next month if things continue going well. 

As well as all the new features we've added, like the customisation of your farm and fixing up of derelict properties, we have also improved areas such as gameplay gating, AI navigation and NPC text. Due to how these all work together in a game as big as ours, we need to do a bit more poking, testing and finessing to make sure it all behaves as expected.

We hope to soon start sharing some behind-the-scenes happenings in the form of a development diary. Some bugs are just too good not to share... oh, the joys of computer game development! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/63bbe186c11876a8ec7035e2a8670491378e9b63.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/581fa3885283c17251a0d2103c0b418548f47613.png[/img]

We love it, really, and we love our 'little' game, which is why we are taking time to get this additional content as good as possible.


All the best,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/b3c6d0707c39c9f57f6dd14a08fd54cf11936db3.png[/img]

Hi,

We have some information for you on the next content drop for Kynseed. We hope to get an Experimental build of our 'Big Build Update' out on Steam in the next couple of weeks or so.

notes.title: New Progress Screen!
notes.content:
Hello there, Kynseed followers!

We understand the importance of providing valuable feedback and guidance whilst you play the game, and we appreciate the feedback from reviews that highlighted the need for better journey representation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/91a364037516b9ac132f2dd17085dec802797001.png[/img]

That's why we're thrilled to introduce the all-new Progress Screen, designed specifically to guide you during your time in Quill.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/ad32f11457f797573f58daabae112e15973d1432.png[/img]

There are twelve carefully curated categories, including both familiar and fresh additions. Here are some noteworthy highlights:

- Challenges: Embark on an extensive new challenge system which rewards you with Brass, items and customisation unlocks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/6ee39cfb41bbb5b4bade8f57a70449253c5dc235.png[/img]

- Lineage: Explore the connections of your family over time, offering a glimpse into your rich familial history.

- Story: Recap your main storyline progress through a step-by-step overview, ensuring you can quickly pick up on your adventure.

- Relationships: Conveniently displayed across a single screen displaying all the characters you've met, along with your friendship levels. Dive deeper for more information.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/0678c1d46923e2dbef0898f8d165d46a2fb8754b.png[/img]

- Items: For avid collectors, the Progress Screen now allows you to get a sense of missing items in your inventory, with silhouettes hinting at what's yet to be found.

- Events: Relive the special occasions you've experienced with a comprehensive record of memorable events.

Additionally, the Progress Screen background itself evolves as you make progress, creating a living piece of art that reflects your journey!

Stay tuned for upcoming videos showcasing these features. In the meantime, we'll continue our work, keeping you updated on more exciting additions and providing insights into the testing, balancing, and release of this '[b]Big Build[/b]' Update.



Best regards,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/71be1a74aa9b812e3434604ccb27aadd3a9595bb.png[/img]

PixelCount

notes.title: Friends & Family in the Big Build Update
notes.content:
Greetings, esteemed Kynseed followers!

Some jobs in Quill are too darn big for you to do alone! Introducing Friends & Family, a substantial new gameplay feature for Kynseed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/50147d34386fc489d979809a60b5da60849f0708.png[/img]

On your farm, you'll have the opportunity to assemble a team of eager friends who will join forces with you to construct larger structures such as composters, tool sheds, greenhouses, and more. You can even breathe new life into a towering windmill, restoring it to its former glory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/3318076f660f0f667927142b76aa9380d7062782.png[/img]

But it doesn't stop there. Abandoned houses are awaiting your attention, ready to be refurbished and made available for new villagers seeking a place to call home.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/9d480563921b38f018dfbb1cda3cdc89f5ad67f0.png[/img]

Recently, Hob attacks have forced some unfortunate villagers into temporary shelter at a village refuge. With the support of your trusted companions, you can help these displaced residents return to their rightful homes, where they truly belong.

And there's more! Rally your best team to mend broken bridges, allowing access across the rivers and unlocking new possibilities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/104ec23359033b4a9e1313173a2cabe7eefda127.png[/img]

This feature is another example of how we've been working hard to join the dots between existing game features, elevating the significance of the relationships you forge with your family and fellow villagers, as well as the valuable items you gather throughout the regions.

Rest assured, our dedication to enhancing the connection with your family, particularly those who have departed Willowdown Farm, remains unwavering. They shall reappear in due time, for those who still walk among the living, that is! More details to follow.

Next, though, we will look at a new Progress Screen.



Warmest regards,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/71be1a74aa9b812e3434604ccb27aadd3a9595bb.png[/img]

PixelCount

notes.title: The Big Build Update!
notes.content:
Greetings, dedicated Kynseed followers!

Today, we are thrilled to share with you the first of many exciting content reveals we have planned. 

Without further ado, we present to you the official name and logo of the update that has occupied our time and efforts since just before the arrival of spring: 'The Big Build Update'!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/9dfbf6a0e4f534c5888513e90f3c57ce07ec6baa.png[/img]


In the upcoming posts, we will be unveiling each new feature individually to avoid spoiling the surprise. However, we can assure you that this game update will introduce three massive game modes and a plethora of quality of life improvements.

Now, let's delve into the essence of our enchanting logo and the significance of its name. What hints can you gather from these delightful elements?

But fear not, dear reader, for we shall return shortly with the announcement of the first new feature, which is - ah, hang on...

Apologies for the brief moment of excitement – I got a little carried away there!


Love,


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/b3c6d0707c39c9f57f6dd14a08fd54cf11936db3.png[/img]

notes.title: Launch Bonus Content!
notes.content:
Dear Seedlings,

As part of our launch celebration and promotion, we are delighted to announce a cheeky treat for our favourite Kynseed players, crafted by our very best castle carpenters.

We bring you the 'Bonus Bog'. 

Now, we are aware that the word 'bog', is a largely British colloquialism, so also consider it our 'Token Toilet', 'Rare Restroom' or  'Wicked WC' .

[previewyoutube=udDhmlxGEw8;full][/previewyoutube]

There are three new exclusive toilet designs to choose from. These are creatively named 'Kid' 'Monster' and 'Nature'.

This is a special bonus for those of you who have already supported us by purchasing Kynseed during Early Access and those future players who purchase the game within one week of launch*. 

These lovingly crafted outhouses will not be available again after December 13th 2022, so don't miss out on your chance to decorate your outhouse...with our colourful designs we mean!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/ce322f66e6ae1ad7ce60d7f1540d6c077ddb89f5.png[/img]


Love,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/b3c6d0707c39c9f57f6dd14a08fd54cf11936db3.png[/img]

notes.title: Kynseed News
notes.content:
Welcome to another parchment of Quillian news, delivered by the news Chaffinches, as the Ravens and Pigeons are on holiday. We have been ferociously working on the game to hammer it into its final shape.

[h3]NPC STORIES[/h3]
One feature we have always been keen on getting in is the idea of ‘NPC Stories’. What are they, you ask in whispered tones?

Each named NPC will say some flavour dialogue at each level gained on friendship, culminating in a bespoke task that you must complete before they 'love' you.

The new dialogue adds a bit of much needed depth and personality to the existing NPCs. Combined with an updated chat system and favours that are tied to their traits, the whole system really helps fill out the characters more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/984212f9b848af83ee605c06e5f066321a772741.gif[/img]
[i]You can find redemption in some NPC stories[/i]

[h3]STORY[/h3]
Speaking of story, we are putting in more of the main story that you all so eagerly want, along with the player's main objective. Just what is your motivation to do the things you need to do? What’s that mysterious noise from the deep woods? What is behind that strange door? Who let the pugs out?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/25cf85f2982b3951c7e5956e06732c0372480a64.gif[/img]
[i]You'll need to get a handle on that door[/i]

[h3]UI[/h3]
One other area of the game which we have been putting a lot of code and art effort into is the User Interface, or UI to those who know their gaming acronyms.

The new UI system is now being implemented for remaining areas, such as the family ledger, shop ledgers and chat systems. 

Using your lovely new ledgers, you will be able to assign shifts, send your family gathering or give them specific orders that will raise their stats via learning...from gardening to studying books.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/bafd9abefe4b0f74a1d9e04324768a3a6d7f4a4e.gif[/img]
[i]Things are looking a bit shifty in the ledger[/i]

[h3]COMBAT[/h3]
We have also been working on combat for Midwood, and Gary has done an absolutely magnificent job with the monsters and their varying anims.

Midwood’s creatures have a very different style to those of Simplewood, and are a bit faster and more aggressive. Get your dodging shoes on!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/9d35aec6eed1820af80124b10e22d25b7d961d40.gif[/img]
[i]Our combat isn't a drag to play[/i]

[h3]WRAP-UP[/h3]
There are lots of other treats being prepared, including the creation of new hubs, a new haven, generations, shop specialisations and more.  So keep an eye out (not literally) for more developer updates in the coming weeks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/1799bfe68f6920ec044b0ccbdbfe41d30556e278.gif[/img]
A big thanks from the team for your continued patience and support.

[b]Happy chocolate egg eating time![/b]

notes.title: Kynseed News
notes.content:
Spring is upon us and the dandelions are out in bloom in Quill.
Picking one, we can see it is time for a little update on what is going on inside the game.
Our industrious team of ten gnomes are tinkering away so here are a couple of things being forged inside their little houses.

[h2]UI UPDATE[/h2]

One of the final elements of the game to get up to launch quality is the User Interface. As such, UI has been a big focus lately, with all of us playing some part in making the menus more consistent, intuitive, and responsive. They also look and feel lovely, like the ferns of Pinehaven.

In addition, we've been making significant progress on many of the remaining screens. This includes the interaction system, which has had an overhaul, with chatting streamlined like one of our finest racing pigs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/c290dde7e0a6d52fabda144d1012b7fb9e9854ff.gif[/img]

Work is also underway on the shop ledgers. When you are sat up late at night, the candle flickering, you need a reliable and informative book to do your accounts and stock. It also helps that it looks great too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/474d93b2a7ef0ab9276c07cc16d4ca35af177413.png[/img]
[i]New look for blacksmith orders in the ledger[/i]

[h3]NEW TITLE SCREEN[/h3]

What is that over there, glinting on the horizon? Why it’s the exciting new title screen based on our brand new Key Art! We can't wait to show you - it is pretty amazing, even if we say so ourselves. Which we just did.

[h2]EVENT EDITOR[/h2]

The second central area of the game we are getting launch-ready is the story and task system, including the main narrative thread and the unique adventures you will embark upon based on the numerous NPCs.

So, to start filling out the game with all the delicious content we need, we created an 'Event and AI behaviour Editor' or ‘EAABE’ for short. We may need to change that acronym.
This drag and drop game design tool allows us to easily create new events and the sim behaviours to support them. We've been replacing events that had previously been 'hard-coded' to now run using the new system, and the benefits to time and bug fixing have been more marvellous than Herbert’s beard. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/6991025bf3b3f0ca102c646c50efeb0b03a4bd5a.png[/img]
[i]This screen shows a few different parts of the tree for a cooking competition event[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/8c55c865b748205050e3e28c6cd460396c4ee048.png[/img]
[i]Each node is a small bit of code with settable properties making it easy to add new ones[/i]

[h3]WHAT'S NEXT?[/h3]

We'll be posting more development updates in the near future, so keep an eye on the news raven to see what fresh produce Quill has to offer!

notes.title: The Oven Ready Cooking Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/05c24d64131b7cff0f73f908ec170ec068eccd46.png[/img]

Greetings Seedings!

What is that smell coming from the castle kitchens?
Hmmmm smells like some sort of freshly baked pie!
Our stomachs are rumbling like distant thunder.
Let's head downstairs and see what's cooking, in the Oven Ready Cooking Update.

[h2]RECIPE BOOK[/h2]
What better way to start your culinary career than with a good old fashioned Recipe Book.
Collect recipes and flick through the jam-encrusted pages in search of marvellous meals.
There are 7, yes SEVEN different cooking minigames to try as you whip up a creamy frenzy of fantastical foodstuffs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/d10ed35014aaf25e204c4ea6a0a1abd665bc0f1c.gif[/img]

[h2]SOUPS[/h2]
Thick, creamy, tasty, homely, simple.
But enough about me!  Let's talk soups.
Simply grind your ingredients in the Hob, before you put it on the hob.
Confused?
Well, it will all make sense.
Just time the arrow to the groove in this simplest of soup-making sections.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/646a8afb019324237f969bb7bd7686ccda32c990.gif[/img]

[h2]STEWS[/h2]
Do people called Stu like stew? Does Stewart make stew art?
How much stew could a Stu stew if a stewing stew could stew stew?
Who knows?
In this minigame, you must choose the ingredients and add them to the pot in the right order.
The timers will flip one by one so try to get them all to finish at the same time!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/bbf75b9f5b22ae877e08958dec0250c5d9ffb353.gif[/img]

[h2]JAMS[/h2]
We're jammin'! 
Yes, preserve your preserves for posterity with the jam making!
Chop up your berries and pop them in the pot before the sands of time run out.
Watch the temperature and always try to keep it balanced.
Hmmm sticky, sweet and jam-packed with goodness.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/d909c33be5c5c833eb4a5611fccb823f0567059f.gif[/img]

[h2]PIES[/h2]
Rollin' rollin' rollin', 
Keep that pastry rollin',
Rollin' rollin' rollin'
Raw dough!
The world is a much better place with pastry on your face.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/5a304e645f692b570a9b514699e341e76248c739.gif[/img]

[h2]PUDDINGS[/h2]
Puddings always bring glad tidings, as well as adding a few inches to the waistline.
Fairly simple to make, just make sure you don't burn them in the kiln.
I just realised I am drooling as I type this, but...must...resist...puddings...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/1263e5c03c9ac233c3f25dabbd90b6be79083e41.gif[/img]

[h2]BREADS[/h2]
Man can not live on bread alone, they say.
You could, if the bread was big enough. You could have a baguette as a table and a nice sourdough chair too. At night, you'd take off your loafers and slip into bread, and your naan would come and tuck you in.
Can you tell that I am hungry?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/0c537ea47eb180d406634f73049ae93c60b3cc07.gif[/img]

[h2]SANDWICHES[/h2]
Sandwiches are the best thing since sliced bread, with a filling.
Invented by the Earl of Sandwich, thousands of years ago, Quillians keep the quaint tradition alive by making some truly disgusting homages to a once noble art.
Can you do any better? Could you create a toastie that won't make even your pigs barf?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/0f4e56783aa523177eb6ac37c0c98c2dc6b4e359.gif[/img]

[h2]UI[/h2]
Cooking is not the only thing included in this lovely update.
We have started overhauling the entire UI!
So expect a new WIP inventory, Status, Task screen and calendar.
We added new banners, task systems, hotbars and all sorts of other goodies.
Please excuse that some of the old UI is still hanging around like a bad smell, but we will get rid of that stink with some freshly baked Apple Bread.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/2794a863ef433f94ad310a5c08ea02b1a1e90fbb.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/1007ea22b495bc8a1ebf72625c472aae7089fba5.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/3587c70e5fd18ccec476106fdda394c0cff6cf7b.gif[/img]

[h2]EVENTS[/h2]
We have spent a good couple of months or so creating a new editor tool that allows us to create events to finally flesh out the land of Quill.
We have 3 such tests of it's power in this update...a weather event, a competition and something a little bit more quirky.
This all paves the way for tons of new story, goals, things to see, things to do, things to mess with and surprises aplenty.
See if you can discover them!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/1216f1a0f4b7a63e8d180c1dacaa8bae370445aa.png[/img]

We also have a few extra lovely bits and bobs in the update...please read the patch notes for more information.
Until next time friends! Happy cooking!

LOVE,
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/a76304561dbf7d648ca64213f01c6d22615755ef.png[/img]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/17823e8e314d9a61a089120f9d0208dde2c626f5.gif[/img]

notes.title: Hag & Slash: The Combat Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/c1044582b8ac7a80ae9d9540e323104743e2678f.png[/img]

Greetings Seedings!

As we look out of the castle window we spy a disturbance in the twisted forests yonder.
Grabbing our telescopes, we spy dark dealings afoot.
Looks like it is time to open up the castle armoury and send cartloads of sharp, pointy weaponry off into the village, where our lovely community of villagers can arm themselves and go sort out the bother, because we are just far too scared.
Why do you think we work in a castle?!

And thus, we welcome you to ‘Hag & Slash: The Combat Update.

[previewyoutube=GmF2YnptNBc;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]OVERVIEW[/h2]
Simplewood is the first of 3 increasingly tricksy places to explore and test your skills against the first set of wonderful denizens we have cooked up for you in our development cauldron.
Within the glades you will find danger, but also some respite and intrigue...a sample of what is to come as we build out the 'fungeons', as we don’t call them.
Within this fabulous update you will also find new Reputation Perks for all your shops, and a lovely little new level to explore, with a very helpful new Master residing within, plus a bunch of fixes and other little bits & bobs.
So get your backpack dusted off, wear reinforced underwear, and prepare for a bit of the old Hag & Slash!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/e9fe1066b6510c685cf864ae383c14d60d353a63.gif[/img]


[h2]SIMPLEWOOD[/h2]
To experience what combat has to offer, enter the depths of Simplewood, the easiest of our dark forests. You will find Simplewood at the top centre of Rivermoor. You should bump into Jogon, who will teach you the way of the blade.
However, if you do not keep your wits about you, then you can be something’s dinner before you can say “Ouch!”
Within each ‘dungeon’ you can elect to go right and stay at the same difficulty, or head deeper in, increasing the difficulty but opening up much more potential for tasty rewards!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/07f6abf2f5c357e6b566d348939eaef9bfc79c28.png[/img]


[h3]LOADOUT[/h3]
Prepare thyself!
Literally. Equip any weapons (up to 2 swords, madam), pack a good meal and stuff up to 10 combat items into your pack.
You can also take in 1 charm and 1 ward which will buff you and debuff your enemies.
If it is night, then maybe a lantern will be handy!
Items can be bought or crafted, and weapons can affect different creatures in different ways.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/0cfcdd1d9a1a1d6a28308fa79e78febe796aa6f4.gif[/img]


[h3]COMBAT[/h3]
Kynseed had a sparkly new combat system that marries the look of a turn-based RPG, but has the reactions and strategy of an action combat game.
Think of it as a mix of One Step From Eden, the Super Mario RPG’s and Steamworld Quest.
You can attack your lane or diagonally adjacent, and each enemy position matches a button on your gamepad.
Combat is ruled by ‘Stamina’, and each attack uses one unit, although there are ways for the skilful to get free hits.
Moving and blocking deplete your stamina so make sure you have enough.
Stamina recharges and the rate of how fast depends on your stamina stat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/c5575df172355e51e7aaad4736094928570da49c.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/5c64add609b8e34164b8291e5bb7ca6a12a496d8.gif[/img]


[h3]PARRY[/h3]

By far the most useful and fun move, Parrying is something you will need to learn if you want to maximise your effectiveness (and it is FUN as we keep saying).
Time a block at just the right moment and you can reflect a projectile back at the slinger, or stop a melee attack and leave them open to a quick counter, the first hit of which is free.
Not everything can be parried though so watch out!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/fa7af7c968f8adf527e2d3b41c5e8baab8acde33.gif[/img]


[h3]THE BOW[/h3]
If you meet Moon the Archery Master, you may get a bow to aid you.
Bows initially don’t cause much damage, but are most effective at knocking enemies out of blocking, draining their stamina and stunning them...buying you time.
You have just 6 arrows per run but may find more on your explorations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/15647eb365df8f9e5e8382d882abc1f00c933431.gif[/img]


[h3]USE ITEMS[/h3]
Those items you packed earlier? Well, you can use them anytime.
Some items can be used on yourself, or thrown onto what we call, ‘Nodes’...the halfway point of a lane between yourself and the enemy.
And some items can be hurled directly at enemies.
Bees.  That’s all we will say.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/4af1d1bbf47700b30004022b9f1567c3f30a150b.gif[/img]


[h3]NON-COMBAT ROOMS[/h3]
As you travel from glade to glade in the forest, you may come across other room types.
These can be anything from little challenges to mysterious interactive elements...we will let you discover these.
You may also find a campfire to heal, although doing so will force you up a few levels of difficulty!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/925040c414438583bcaf6b8158d74ef24524193c.gif[/img]

The update also contains a new region called Drownhill and some extra work on making the 3 shop types fun.
You can now raise reputation to earn perk points that you can spend on...you guessed it...Perks!
This is just the start of improving the business aspect of the game.
You will also find more proverbs filled in and a number of other fixes and little nuggets as detailed in the changelist which our scribe scrabbled to scribble.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/bdd88ab82ea3064588bd2ae35ed3acd1d0c0c226.gif[/img]

We can’t wait to hear your feedback and watch your videos and streams as you battle the first set of foes in an update we are intensely proud of.
We poured a lot of hard work and love into this, and jugs of coffee into ourselves, just so we could send you to do our dirty work in the dark forest.
We want a cut of the loot by the way.

Until next time friends!

notes.content:
Hello there seedlings!

The latest update Hag & Slash: The Combat Update is now available and here is the changelog of what has been updated!  As always, these things are an ongoing development, so expect bugs, balancing issues and an overwhelming urge to sprinkle herbs on things.

We appreciated any feedback at our usual channels on Discord, our forums or in the Steam Discussions. 

[h2][b][u]Cʜᴀɴɢᴇʟᴏɢ[/u][/b][/h2]
🔷 Combat completely redone into a Reactive Realtime Combat system
ᅠᅠ🔷 Head to Simplewood, at the top of Rivermoor to meet Jogon, Master of Combat and learn the way of the sword
ᅠᅠ🔷 Fight against 5 enemy types with multiple abilties to figure out
ᅠᅠ🔷 Equip a loadout of two swords, a ward/charm, 10 combat items and a meal
ᅠᅠ🔷 Choose your strategy carefully where death can cost you fairweather tax years of your life!
ᅠᅠ🔷 Take your dog into battle for help
ᅠᅠ🔷 Pick Combat items in paused mode to aid in attack, defense and healing
ᅠᅠ🔷 Travel deeper into the forest for tougher difficulty with better rewards
ᅠᅠ🔷 Some areas allow for rest and little minigames for additional loot
🔷 Drownhill, a new region in Summerdown to explore
ᅠᅠ🔷 Includes Moon - learn how to use a bow from our latest Master
🔷 Can order some fresh goods for the good store

🔷 Shop reputation levelling reworked with perk points unlocked as reputation goes up with 10 perks per shop
🔶 Apothecary crafting adjusted to be easier.  Branded or offbrand results from curing all or partial traits
🔶 Apothecary ailments/maladies based on season along with shop reputation level
🔶 Apothecary crafting with no patient and recipe set now crafts combat items
🔶 Setup for blacksmith orders to be based on reputation level and also cover all 5 available ore types
🔶 Ledger UI updated
🔶 Various level tweaks mainly for collision, nav and layering
🔶 Counter staff should display thinking dots while deciding the response to customers
🔶 Blacksmith orders collected with self service due to a closed shop will still provide some rep
🔶 Blacksmith shelf browser customers served by a worker when you have no shelf items will provide a placebo item with similar 50/50 chance of gaining a little rep and brass or losing a little rep

notes.title: Gathering Storm Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/4d9ffd3b3cc665bf78bc398c45ed6533461e4dce.gif[/img]

Greetings Seedings!

It’s that time again, when we lower the castle portcullis and send our excitable update sheep down the road into our community.
This fabulous update is a feast for the eyes and ears, as well as being packed with mystery and story.
Over the next few weeks, we will reveal more about the next update as our sheep reaches ramming speed as it charges down the hill towards the dark forest. 
Judging by the helmet that our sheep is wearing, it would seem that there is going to be a bit of rough n tumble and the apothecary might need to stock up on wound treatments! 
As for now, let’s have a look inside the Gathering Storm update, that we proudly present to you.



[u][b][h3]WEATHER & LIGHTING[/h3][/b][/u]
Probably the stars of the show are our new lighting and weather systems.
Rain, fog, wind, heat and snow bring a level of immersion to Quill that takes the game to ambient heights.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/c764adf6b47f396ff47209664033f1ec33ebd68f.gif[/img]

[u][b][h3]WIND[/h3][/b][/u]
A light breeze or a full-on gale. The Goddesses provide.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/75f6d76ab5c4a63c275ac4898a26887609653525.gif[/img]


[u][b][h3]RAIN[/h3][/b][/u]
Rain has various intensities, from “It’s spitting!” to “I love storms!”
Our resident weather coding expert Nick, also made it so it does not rain indoors, and the sound changes whether you are near bodies of water, near greenhouses and when you are snug inside.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/07294a95a8118b8005eb6c2b4de8e02754eebf45.gif[/img]


[u][b][h3]SNOW[/h3][/b][/u]
Ahhh a lovely crisp winter’s day. The tingle of a snowflake on your nose. The blast of icy death as a blizzard whacks you in the face.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/cc326bee592856a205f9d69b2f83a292e50502b6.png[/img]


[u][b][h3]FOG[/h3][/b][/u]
From morning mists to creepy pea-soupers to colourful Fae rainbow clouds, you can’t beat fog for sheer atmosphere. Some say it is Dragon’s breath. Others say it is a visible aerosol of tiny water droplets. Some people are less fun than others. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/6b30a80660e0182b115f0a1b0cf5a7ce25024b0a.png[/img]

[u][b][h3]LIGHTS & LANTERNS[/h3][/b][/u]
Lights now contain themselves in houses. We tweaked the times of day and more importantly, made the lantern really cool and actually useful.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/37decd95d105f6aa362642e3ad121233baa093bd.gif[/img]

[u][b][h3]A NEW PET[/h3][/b][/u]
Introducing the FILIFRYTH!
This magnificent and strange bushy owl is not so easy to tame, unless you know the way.
But what is the ability that this odd yet cute little creature has?
We are not telling you because that would be taking the Piscatootle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/bfcf803ea8d1da9acf388329e29d8a3f7e8023e7.gif[/img]


[u][b][h3]NEW INTRO & MAJOR PROLOGUE CHANGES[/h3][/b][/u]
Yes, we added some initial mystery and set up to the story, changed a ton of dialogue and moved tasks around. There will be fun. There will be shocks. There will be fear. There will be blood.  Just kidding, that’s a great movie.

[u][b][h3]FAE REALM OF EVERGREEN[/h3][/b][/u]

Find the method to unlock it, and you can visit the lush forests of Evergreen. Strange noises drift from ancient trees and bizarre denizens wander amongst the whispering trees and gentle streams with their discordant music.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/3a0975ae9c80a95ae7d719bf32c870b4c1ffaa28.gif[/img]


The update also contains delights such as a new region transition system, various tweaks and polish and an absolute ton of bug fixes. We also probably introduced an absolute ton more too.

Some of you with high awareness stats may have noticed a very modest price rise on the Store page. We felt the added content to date justified a small raise, and this will help keep the Castle Guards from revolting. Some of them are already revolting, but their mother's love them.

We can’t wait to hear your feedback and see your screenshots and watch your streams.
So immerse yourself, wrap up warm and experience the elements of our brand new update, brought to you by the hard-working Gnomes of PixelCount (they tried to form a union, but were hungry so formed an onion).

Until next time friends!

LOVE,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/5daf40181b805683f544eb17cf6af23fba8bea07.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/1afaf4026ba70067c11fb4f41251e24c793fbcf2.gif[/img]

notes.title: Dev Update: Singing the theme for a hospital
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/4d9ffd3b3cc665bf78bc398c45ed6533461e4dce.gif[/img]

Greetings Seedlings!

The Apothecary Update is finally out and budding healers are getting their eager hands on their pestles, and giving things a good mash.

The update was a little bit slow to appear due to a large re-design of how parts of the apothecary worked...poor Nick was up to his eyeballs trying to make sense of our documents and discussions!
The team pulled through with a fantastic base we can build on, and with your valued feedback we can shape this very unique business into er...shape.

What is also very cool to come from this is that the UI developments, and the minigame mechanics made for the various apothecary stations, can now be utilised elsewhere, especially in regards to the cooking minigames.

Eventually you will be able to chop up your carrots, stir your stews and juice your berries like a regular Gordon Ramsbottom.

"Hey! PixelCount team! What's in the next update?" you shout, while keeping one eye on your boiling cauldron. Well we have a whole new section of intro to add, which will give a more exciting and mysterious start. The Prologue is having a fine tune, with brand new dialogue, character edits, story tweaks and tasks moved about etc.

We also want to set Nick and Mr Weekes free on the lighting and weather systems to bring our visuals and atmosphere bang up to date, to increase your immersion and make the world feel even better. Going beyond that, NPC stories to add depth, a spanky new top secret combat system, having kids and nurturing their little minds are all in our development sights.

As always we thank you for your amazing support and patience, and now in this latest update, patients.
Below is a little look at some of the treasures you can find within the game right now...


[u][b][h3]PATIENT DIAGNOSIS[/h3][/b][/u]
Open your Apothecary and the NPCs of the world will come in with a variety of ailments.
Listen to their problems and try to work out how best to counter those bad Traits that are afflicting them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/3241e6e8430555cfdab3fa7d251c0e8023374916.gif[/img]

[u][b][h3]THE MEDICAL TOME[/h3][/b][/u]
Use your own knowledge or if wanting to speed things up, you can refer to a fine book that will tell you some of the recipes needed to cure various maladies.
Powders, Creams and Potions are available to view with any unlocked knowledge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/657dc785c7be3166610912228a6329c97ad09e8c.gif[/img]

[u][b][h3]CRAFTING POWDERS[/h3][/b][/u]
You can mix a nice Powder by chopping and grinding your ingredients and then mashing them with the pestle. Try and find all the crunchy bits to ensure a fine powder that will soothe your patient's problems in no time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/6f462ed6647a13978086c172123640995f0cb947.gif[/img]

[u][b][h3]CRAFTING CREAMS[/h3][/b][/u]
If it is something superficial, then perhaps a Cream will suffice?
Turn on the Bunsen burners and keep stirring to check consistency.
On the left, the extract seeps from your ingredients and emerges as concentrated drops of healing goodness.
On the right, wax to thicken. Don't make it too runny or too thick!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/0b74b2e419cfc207f7de88df95a426ebd32a5d8c.gif[/img]

[u][b][h3]CREATING POTIONS[/h3][/b][/u]
A more magical malady plaguing your patrons?
Then you need a fine potion.
Stick your ingredients in the crusher to extract that lovely juice.
Pour into the pot and watch the reaction.
Ice forming?  Turn up the heat. Bubbles? Turn down the heat.
Check the colour chart and find the correct reagent dispenser of the opposite colour to the smoke to neutralise the reaction.
Grind, pull and squirt your way to success!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/5986deb6b7c96b40f33186132b83d8aa1bd35e80.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/ef50b147fe4bc39af41d87242d2beb99edc03870.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/395fe2f928154c0731548f7eb23a2bc8fed12de1.gif[/img]

[u][b][h3]MR FAIRWEATHER'S NEW STOCK[/h3][/b][/u]
As well as the Apothecary, there are some nice new items from our Fae friend to consider.
Below are three such items, Mirror Mirror, Waterman's Reminder, and the Vase of Forgiveness.
You can also buy Forget-Me-Yet seeds, Judith's Charming Charmer Charm and the brilliantly useful Turdis. 
Just don't use the latter one if someone else hasn't flushed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/81070de01117db482964bf5d25f54b249f20218e.gif[/img]

notes.title: The Relationship Update!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/5aa91a3dd9aae524b80a3e046f3210e3fcc7fdf9.gif[/img]

Hello again purveyors of fine gaming. While everyone else is celebrating scary things, it seems we're over here celebrating...[i]*checks notes*[/i]...love! (Unless you find commitment scary, I suppose.) [strike]Witch[/strike] which is to say, the long awaited Relationship Update has been released!

Here at Castle PixelCount we have been stewing this very large update over a very long time. At long last, we are pleased to finally pour the contents of the cauldron into the phial, ready for you all to have a sip of. Along the way we also recently hired not [b][url=https://twitter.com/Kynseed/status/1316004063868223488]one[/url][/b] but [b][url=https://twitter.com/Kynseed/status/1316063118439653383]two[/url][/b] passing Tinkers (colloquially known as programmers) and their expertise has added some extra special froth to the brew.

The amount of people now milling about our castle is growing. The excitement in the dusty corridors and damp, gloomy vaults is palpable. You could palp it if you wanted. So as the sun rises over this latest update, we are all filled with a new energy, inspired partly by our new helping hands but also by our amazing, growing community. Without your little faces peering at us across the moat from your little cottages, we wouldn’t even open the shutters. We look forward to you joining us on the next stage of the adventure and to enjoy the fare we cooked up in the Cauldron of Development.

Though for today, we shall give you a highlight of some of the changes you can expect to find in this latest update concoction of ours. The Relationship Update has been a long time coming and is actually many incremental updates combined into one. (You can check out all those incremental updates [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/758870/discussions/0/1748980761802478102/][b]here[/b][/url] if you like.) So feel free to peruse the highlight's delights below.

[u][b][h1]CHANGELOG HIGHLIGHTS[/h1][/b][/u]
[u][b][h3]Building NPC Relationships[/h3][/b][/u]You can now befriend NPC's through your actions (or, you know, make a few enemies too). Much like in real life, it'll take more than just gift giving to build lasting relationships with those around you.[list][*]Players can reach adulthood where you can date and marry suitable partners if your friendship level is high enough
[*]All the mortal NPC's in the game fully age, so you can find the perfect someone among the 60 or so villagers currently in the game[*]Many newly added NPC reactions to the player's actions[*]A collection of noticeboard tasks to help raise your friendship level and earn you some rewards
[*]NPC's will react to things like the weather and sometimes gossip[/list]


[u][b][h3]Marrying NPC's[/h3][/b][/u]The land of Quill is one of tradition and the process of marriage is no different.[list][*]After building up to love in friendship, there's a seven-step tradition for marriage culminating in your wedding day
[*]After marrying, your partner will live on your farm and carry out tasks as organised in the Family Ledger (which can include helping out with feeding the animals, cooking, farming, and gathering fruit on the farm)
[*]You can send out your partner on gathering trips to find resources and return home with them
[*]Your spouse will comment on the state of your marriage, farm, and wealth (or lack of it)[/list]


[u][b][h3]Item Improvements[/h3][/b][/u]Another area that's seen a fair bit of improvements are the plethora of items in the game.[list][*]Many of the items now have multiple star rating versions to obtain based on conditions that can be discovered or uncovered from NPC's 
[*]Higher rated items help with better boons from offerings, fulfilling tasks, earning more money, and a better friendship increase from NPC's
[*]Proverbs also help to locate the many growables and fish out there in the world
[*]A multitude of delicious new recipes added to the game
[*]Many properties for items are now in place[/list]


[u][b][h3]Continuing Improvements to Presentation[/h3][/b][/u]Visual polish and presentation work is a constant process for a game in development. Here's a handful of areas we've recently turned our attention to.[list][*]Minimap now shows locations, dating spots, and homes
[*]A plethora of UI improvements, especially within the inventory and chat boxes
[*]Upgraded to MonoGame 3.7 (the framework our engine is built on) which brings with it a more elegant handling of different screen aspect ratios[/list]


[u][b][h3]Full Changelogs[/h3][/b][/u]As always, there's vastly more additions and fixes made than we can list here. So jump on over to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/newshub/app/758870/view/5411597309545114939][b]this recent changelog of ours[/b][/url] to check out the details or just drop by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/758870/discussions/0/1748980761802478102/][b]our changelog repository thread[/b][/url] to see the myriad of smaller incremental updates over recent months that have gone into this Relationship Update.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/3d4d700b9e819855b8b283a6ee1f23d9d8ffa4d5.gif[/img]
[u][b][h1]OTHER BITS AND BOBS[/h1][/b][/u]
[u][b]Family Brounie[/b][/u]
Pott the Brounie will offer guidance and insults in equal measure, while helping keep your farm tidy.

[u][b]Skin Customisation[/b][/u]
The player can now choose from skin tones to add to their hair colour choices. (This is just a first pass at this, but more customisation options are still likely to come.)

[u][b]Goddess Offering Rework[/b][/u]
A cool, strategic new system for gaining boons, blessings, jinxes, and curses!

[u][b]Gift Mails[/b][/u]
NPC's will send you gifts if they are particularly fond of you.

[u][b]Family Secret Boxes[/b][/u]
Discover the codes to unlock a variety of heirlooms, from secret recipes to valuable information.

[u][b]Fertiliser[/b][/u]
Scoop the poop to enhance and speed up your crop growing.

[u][b]Equipment Experience[/b][/u]
Your tools can be levelled up with use, bestowing extra bonuses.

[u][b]Milling[/b][/u]
Not enough grinding in the game? Use these stones in a windmill to grind to your heart's content.

[u][b]Marshtyt the Master Gardener[/b][/u]
Meet this cheeky chappie who can teach you how to sow your seeds effectively.


[u][b][h1]UNTIL NEXT TIME[/h1][/b][/u]
Next on our game development journey we'll be moving on to more exciting and long-awaited features such as combat, Apothecary ownership, having children, and a plethora of other wonderful delights.

As always, a most heartfelt thanks to all of you for your support and the myriad of ways you give it - whether by sending in bugs, leaving a review letting us know what you think, hanging out in the community, or just by simply playing our game. This community genuinely means the world to us and all this would be quite literally impossible without each of you. Take care friends and we'll meet again further down the road.

Love,
[i]PixelCount[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/4b6dfd3cf00a861bf40e92b5f468edec1a3a4778.gif[/img]

notes.content:
ᅠᅠ

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/6712b09aed588c033c3b752155e35abc1ea8627c.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/900263e07e36db3d81a48d44e2f7c10aaf75258c.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/3abace8efb5be8cd0aab40d2680d88c9f52ff39a.png[/img]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/74d1c6eb5d567ba30622a02422d72479468249ee.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/06fc66225573d5e4d9778b03ce1d228aee8fc4ee.png[/img]

Well hello again and welcome back! There's been some interesting developments since last we talked.

Regarding game developments, Charlie has been busy doing another pass over the Evergreen and Woemarsh regions. He's also been working on some new Reputation systems that'll determine how the player accrues Rep for not just their shops but also their family. As usual, check out the individual updates below for the details.

Regarding other developments, we're rather excited to report that we've recently begun looking to add another coder to our team! Doing so will no doubt have sweeping benefits to the game's progress and we're both happy and humbled to have reached a place where we can expand our small team. So read on below and we'll tell you all about it!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/557237772250ec6a6e2df974880a14da2d3e0183.png[/img]
[url=https://twitter.com/lionbum][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/97520b158c448b3b69e9e51d1805bdf0f51eb484.png[/img][/url]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/06fc66225573d5e4d9778b03ce1d228aee8fc4ee.png[/img]

It's been a bit of a full-on time since our last posts. As Neal will go into detail about, we set about trying to recruit a coder and conducting some interviews. It was really interesting, though sometimes a challenge for me to understand what on Earth they were talking about with all their coder jargon.

What is clear is that there are many really talented people out there and I am jealous of their skillz. I was part of the meetings as a 'gauge of character' and to see if they would fit into the team as a whole. We have a very close team with great camaraderie and that does need to be considered as well as coding prowess and a bit of flair.

Aside from that I have been finishing up a pass of Evergreen, starting Woemarsh, and finally trying to sort out the Reputation system. It was a challenge as we don't want to force the player down certain paths. In summary, we have two Rep systems: one per shop and then one for all shops, friendships, and deeds (called your Family Rep). The former will unlock Perks that help your shop and the latter unlocks benefits beyond just shops. Both Reps come with tiers of renown, from Unknown to Legendary. The UI for this then needed mocking up in [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Visio][b]Visio[/b][/url], which was slow going. I find I always forget one thing here and there.

Got potentially exciting times ahead and hoping we can get the coder onboard and get more features out. We appreciate your patience with this game. There is lots to do, but lots of good stuff, and you will only benefit from more updates. Stay safe everyone!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/b4510579a1b378825a25c55a72acb777f353f5c5.png[/img]
[url=https://twitter.com/sporadic_words][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/a1eeb693dd10483ee52ddd4fd9e85af81dc6a898.png[/img][/url]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/b5943e6e93182f17c7970bcc69476e16bb05528f.png[/img]

Another month zips by with a slower pace still as we start on the process of hiring an additional coder. It's a decision we've been thinking on for a few years now where we actually came very close to getting somebody prior to Early Access but timing just didn't work out. Though in connection with recent business developments, it has become a possibility again and so we opened up applications and were pleasantly surprised to see such a large response compared to our expectations!

There's also been a bunch of feedback requests from candidates which I've been trying to go through one by one to give specific advice to each person's submissions. That said, it feels like maybe there are some common threads I could mention here on the off chance anyone is reading and interested. (A small disclaimer that this is my first time recruiting a coder so my experience is limited to what we are specifically looking for, but hopefully there is something of use still!)

[i][b]Note from the Editor:[/b] For any non-coders who want to follow along, I've added explanatory links for some of the terms used below.[/i]

[b][u]#1 - GETTING TO THE GOOD STUFF[/u][/b]
The first important bit is about presentation and minimising the time it takes to get to the good parts. While most applicants did include portfolio or itchio links, there were quite a few that relied on links to web games to play rather than any video reel or brief articles describing the work they did. Chances are that people hiring aren't able to play most of these web games because of time constraints; the more applicants the less practical it becomes and the more you'll lose the chance to impress quickly. It's similar to advertising a game I guess in that sense. You need a sizzle reel of a minute or two that gets to the point quickly and some screenshots that helps gauge the quality. In a related sense, linking the presentation to the role being applied for is helpful too for showing relevant skills. For example, many people who applied have a background in [url=https://unity.com/][b]Unity[/b][/url] which is fine for roles using that but presents a challenge in our situation where our code uses the [url=https://www.monogame.net/][b]MonoGame[/b][/url] framework. The clearer it was from the covering mail or website that their experience ran deeper on having worked on their own engine, used [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_XNA][b]XNA[/b][/url]/MonoGame in the past, released commercial games, demonstrated more advanced Unity usage (maybe developing their own plugin/editor), the better. Such applicants moved towards the top of the pile, as it demonstrated existing experience that would suggest they could do well in the role and that they understood the role they were applying for.

[b][u]#2 - EASILY VERIFIABLE CODE[/u][/b]
Second is seeing source code and [url=https://github.com/][b]github[/b][/url] usage, which gives me a good sense of how a person has worked on prior projects. Lots of bonus points to ones where there is a project with a bunch of [url=https://www.quora.com/What-exactly-does-committing-code-mean-and-how-is-it-done-at-different-companies][b]commits[/b][/url] for the project. A surprising amount of applicants I found included [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_source-code-hosting_facilities][b]repos[/b][/url] where there was an initial commit and that was it (the only repo updated was the website portfolio one). Personally I found this a bit disconcerting as it just leaves a big project to scour through with no true sense of how it was worked on (including the sceptical wondering of knowing if it was one person's sole work). It also links in with #1 that scouring through means it is taking a lot of time to try and find the good parts. First impressions are really important cause you just don't know the circumstance of when it'll be seen and how much or little time might be spent looking at it.

[b][u]#3 - PORTFOLIO POLISH[/u][/b]
Third is about quality of the portfolio. Once you've caught my eye enough to look through video/screenshots (and maybe play if time permits), the next thing I'm looking for is how polished/solid/creative/innovative each presented bit is. A lot of 'professional' game development is about spending the time on those details. Perhaps some examples might help illustrate some common features of projects that don't catch the eye:
[list][*]A character jumps in a platformer and looks weightless.
[*]Standing on a slope and feeling like it has no effect (again, from a weightless point of view where you'd perhaps expect sliding, friction, different animation, etc.).
[*]The camera being fixed on the center of the player the whole time.
[*]Power-ups collected that just disappear without any visual/audio cue.
[*]Menus/levels/UI being really static and not guiding the eye at all.
[*]Clones of things like Tetris/Snake/Asteroids where there's no difference to the originals. (Funnily enough, part of my application to Lionhead was from a Tetris clone but I had included an extra twist of bomb pieces and adding falling blocks to the menu screen to liven it up which managed to do the job some 17 years ago!)[/list]
Hopefully the list above gives a few ideas of the ways of making the difference in quality that helps show understanding of what it takes to finish a game. If we were in the first year or two of development maybe we wouldn't be quite as picky on this front, but this role is all about helping us finish the game. Basically, every little bit helps in terms of showing attention to detail and persistence in effort. So to be efficient on a portfolio it can be about choosing the right parts to concentrate on, as obviously completing every piece to commercial quality would take too long (and you might as well be looking to sell the game at that point!). I find making a short video or GIF of something I work on, then reviewing [i]just[/i] that video or GIF, often helps a lot on that front as it creates that distance of perspective where you can look at the game without being immersed in the controls.

As other advice on this point, I'd recommend checking out the best games that are the same genre to what you are making for ideas of the little touches. Seeking out tutorials on YouTube or various game dev sites can also help with the implementation details and providing pre-packaged research. ([url=https://www.youtube.com/user/McBacon1337][b]Game Maker's Toolkit[/b][/url] on YouTube is particularly useful for this I think.) The challenge in just following the lead of others though is it shows a level of competency but there is a lack of flair/innovation to make your own mark. So it is also important to consider how you can show your own originality in combination with polish as it will help stand out and reach the top of the pile.

I think those three points probably cover the basics to go over so I'll leave it there for now! It's been really humbling/inspiring seeing all the applicants and having the chance to interview some as well. For now we're still in the final stages of the hiring process and handling the business developments but hopefully we'll soon have more to announce on all that!

To wrap up quickly on actual game development progress (as time permitted amongst the coder hiring process): since the update in the middle of August I've been working mostly on items and recipe setup along with some bug fixes. I've also started work on the player children setup, which is exciting. (To set expectations, this is early days stuff so will take a few months to reach a public build.) Apart from that, work is continuing on all the polish/improvements for the relationship update which is now starting to see long-standing in-progress items ticked off but there's still plenty to do which I better get back to. 'Til next time, wishing everyone all the best!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/fe7a04f5f6c7202f6df1f6f3f4e64a8cea860030.png[/img]
[url=https://twitter.com/MrMatthewAllen][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/06b82480560fa97fac6005c38b69a62e8e3f99e4.png[/img][/url]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32044784/b5943e6e93182f17c7970bcc69476e16bb05528f.png[/img]

As my cohorts mentioned above, the lion's share of our time in these recent weeks has been spent on looking for another coder to add to the team. As is often the case, focusing on the business side of this project always tends to require a fair amount of our available time and focus, thereby causing game development to take more of a back seat than we'd like. (If it were possible I imagine we'd prefer to never stop working on the game, living in some sort of perpetual business-free utopia.) Yet this time we don't terribly mind it cause the business at hand is to find someone whose [i]sole[/i] job is to help code.

This is incredibly exciting for us, because up 'til now we've been chiefly running as a skeleton crew. As such, most of us share multiple roles on the team which forces us to divide our time and focus between the various (and often large) workloads of each role. For example, Neal has been not just our one and only programmer but he also manages much of the business and finances. (Taxes, payroll, expense management, and so on.) So adding another person to assist purely with code will have a huge impact for a small team like ours. Ultimately, it'll help improve the quality of the game and the efficiency with which we make it.

Originally, my plan for this [i]Post[/i] was to collate some interesting community stats for you all to check out (sourced from overall community analytics as well as our recent player survey.) Though as often happens with best laid plans, my focus got diverted elsewhere due to us recently starting this hiring process. Hiring some help for the code has always been something we've considered since before Early Access, but as a small team just starting out we often didn't have the resources to make it happen. Yet it always stayed on our minds as a "maybe one day" type of goal.

Thus, it seems that day has arrived. So once we decided we were finally at a good place to expand our little team, we wanted to move on it rather quickly. The first order of business was that I needed to create a new jobs page on our website along with posting the position itself. We wanted to not only explain the job adequately but also show a bit of our personality as a studio. Making sure we hire someone who "got" our vibe and culture as a developer was super important to us. ([url=https://pixelcountstudios.com/jobs/][b]Here's how that page turned out[/b][/url], for anyone interested.)

In addition to this, I helped set up a sort of pipeline for our application process. Namely this just meant setting emails up to funnel applicants to some designated areas of our master inbox on Outlook and to help provide Neal with any support or assistance he might need (because as a coder, he's ultimately the one who'd need to be replying to and organizing coder candidates).

From there, we then shared the job post in a few spots around the community as well as other social channels. We didn't really know what sort of response to expect, but I do know we were keeping our expectations pretty conservative. Yet the quantity (and even quality) of responses received were well above anything we had anticipated, which was encouraging and humbling. Of course, the more responses there were the more initial work this represented as it meant there were more candidates to go through, reply to, and interview. (We were also very keen on not being a sort of cold silent company during this process and so it was important to us that we took the time to not just view every candidate's response but to also give an individual followup reply to each regardless of our decision.)

I found that during this process my mind was very much put into the mode of thinking about how our game and company might seem to a new-hire joining for the first time. What internal processes might possibly need polishing or updating? Is all our project's internal file sharing still up to snuff, for example? What other such areas might need attention? In addition to this, working on the new jobs page of our site got me thinking about how some of our website was in dire need of updating, both on the front end and back. Similarly, adding yet another email address to our server's already long list (addresses for team members, bug reports, community accounts, job applicants most recently, and so on) reminded me of our myriad of server-side email forwarders I have set up and how our master Outlook inbox could probably stand to get somewhat reorganized.

This then sent me on a bit of a twisting path in which I assessed such areas and found there were many things I felt needed updating. That said, I've rattled on a fair bit already for one update, so I'll graciously save you all from enduring a detailed explanation of all these individual updates I got into. Perhaps I'll touch lightly on it in the next issue for anyone particularly interested. Long story short, I've had my hands unexpectedly full with such work these past number of weeks.

Still, the time we're spending on these business things [i]now[/i] will yield rewards for the game [i]later[/i]. Once we finish the final remaining steps of this hiring process, we'll finally have some extra hands helping out on the code - something which will no doubt have a significant positive impact on the game. It's a most interesting time for our team to be sure and I look forward to offering more updates on these things in our next issue of [i]The Post[/i]. Until then, much love to you all!
